newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two foreign suitors eye Mexico's Banca Confia.
newsitem.headline: Two foreign suitors eye Mexico's Banca Confia.

text.p: Two foreign firms are mulling the possibility of buying part of Banca Confia, the main subsidiary of Grupo Financiero Abaco, as part of efforts to recapitalize the stricken bank.
Officials at Principal International Group as well as Citicorp's Citibank said negotiations were underway, though no final decisions had been made.

Confia needs around $250 million in capital. Like other banks it was hard hit by Mexico's 1995 economic crisis, and it has to replenish its capital base as part of commitments to the government that bought a chunk of its troubled loans.

Jan Jobe, president of Des Moines-based Principal International Group, told Reuters that though it had set up a joint pension fund with Abaco called Afore Confia-Principal, it has still not made a decision on a Confia purchase.

"We haven't made any decisions about purchasing. We are looking for a possibility for investing. We haven't set any specific timeline, but we will be continuing to work on it throughout the summer," he said.
A Citibank official, who asked not to be identified, said negotiations with Monterrey-based Abaco were underway, but he said there was no target date for a deal.
Analysts said they doubted Citibank would go through with a purchase, believing it may prefer to take over Mexico's intervened bank Banpais instead.
